name: SE Ranking
verdict: No OAuth: each customer creates an API key in their API Dashboard and pastes it in. Embedding SE Ranking data in your own product needs sales permission, so check that before building.
needGuide: No — just collect each customer's API key, but ask SE Ranking sales first if you embed its data.

auth.detail: Send Authorization: Token <key> (a ?apikey= query parameter also works). One key covers the Data and Project APIs. There is no developer-registered OAuth. Their hosted MCP server (https://api.seranking.com/mcp) offers OAuth 2.1 browser sign-in for MCP clients, or an X-Api-Key header. Keys have full account access; read-only keys are not yet available.

effort.timeToProduction: Same day for own use; unknown if sales permission is needed to embed data

approval.gate: No approval for using your own key. Embedding SE Ranking data in a third-party product is a non-standard use: the commercial-use page says to book a demo or contact sales for permission, and direct competitors need explicit consent. Customers who want their own data would supply their own key.

scopes.why: No scopes: keys have full account access.
scopes.summary: None. Keys have full account access across the Data, Project, Local Marketing and SE Visible APIs. The MCP server does not expose every endpoint.

cost: API access is included in every platform plan (Essential, Pro, Business, Core, Growth, Enterprise); monthly Data API credits are 10k, 25k, or 100k depending on plan. Standalone Data API credit packs are annual, lowest tier 12M credits for $2,148/yr.
prerequisites: Account and owner: Use a company-owned master account; API access belongs to the master account.
Where you register: Log in, click the API icon in the left nav, then Dashboard, then + CREATE API KEY, name it, and click CREATE KEY

Cost: API access is included in every platform plan (Essential, Pro, Business, Core, Growth, Enterprise); monthly Data API credits are 10k, 25k, or 100k depending on plan. Standalone Data API credit packs are annual, lowest tier 12M credits for $2,148/yr.

registerAt.path: Log in, click the API icon in the left nav, then Dashboard, then + CREATE API KEY, name it, and click CREATE KEY

steps.do: Confirm the account plan includes API access (API icon in the left nav)
Create a key at API Dashboard, then + CREATE API KEY; use one key per environment
Build the client with Authorization: Token <key> against the Data and Project APIs
Add a key-validation call to the account subscription endpoint (0 credits) in your connect flow
Contact sales (demo or contact page) if your product displays SE Ranking data to third parties
Store customer-pasted keys encrypted and track credit usage per customer

roles.team: Use a company-owned master account; API access belongs to the master account.
roles.console: none documented (no role restrictions on key creation were stated; multiple keys per account are allowed)
roles.customer: The customer generates a key in their own API Dashboard and pastes it into your app. Sub-account users cannot use OAuth in MCP and must get the key from the account administrator.

testing: Use a Postman collection and a free trial account (whether trials include API access is not stated).
Only 2xx responses use credits, and the account subscription endpoint costs 0 credits, so use it to validate a pasted key.

blockers.fix: Tell customers a pasted key grants everything, and warn that restricted keys are not yet available.

blockers.problem: Sub-account users cannot use OAuth-based MCP
blockers.fix: Ask the master account holder for a key.

blockers.problem: Credits are consumed per request and per record
Embedding data in a customer-facing product may need written permission from sales

automation.agentCan: Write the API client, key-validation call and credit tracking, run test calls, and draft the sales request for commercial embedding.
automation.humanMust: Create or own the account, buy a plan or credit pack, and ask SE Ranking sales for commercial or embedded-use permission.

uncertain: Whether trial accounts include API access, rate limit numbers, role requirements for key creation, and whether the MCP OAuth supports third-party clients beyond Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor.
